fixes: P1 (mattes; the keyframe itself is fine): the claim that each flame layer over its unlit layer reproduces the candle is not true at the wick junction. I composited flame over unlit and compared it with the full candle. The left candle differs in about 61 px, the right in 42 and the 4:3 chamberstick in 50. Alpha is off by up to 0.25, and premultiplied RGB by up to 58/255 (bounding boxes, 16:9 left x48-60/y711-721, right x2494-2506/y722-730, 4:3 chamberstick around x291-304/y1344-1385). During the ignite and relight beats (f1612-f1707) the eye goes straight to that spot, so a 25 % alpha hole or excess at the flame root will flicker. Fix: build the unlit layer first (full candle with the flame region inpainted), then solve the flame layer as the exact residual: alpha_f = 1 - (1 - a_full)/(1 - a_unlit) clamped, and RGB unpremultiplied from full minus unlit times (1 - alpha_f). Then assert that over(flame, unlit) equals full to within 1/255 in handoff.py.

P2 (mattes): unlit wick tips carry a leftover grey 'flame-root' disc. It is most obvious on the 4:3 chamberstick (table_edge_bottom_unlit) at 5x, and still reads as a grey blob at 1-2x. The flame layers also carry a pale grey ghost under the flame body, plus stray orange specks to the left of the left candle's flame (visible over light grey). Fix: paint or clone a short charred, slightly curled wick tip into the *_unlit layers. In the *_flame layers, zero the alpha of any pixel below the flame's luminous core that is dimmer than about 0.4 in luminance, so the flame layer is clean over any background.

P3 (encode guard): the blank parchment field (259,350 to 1195,1350 px) is the game's 260x340 texture stretched about 3.9x. It is extremely low-frequency: Laplacian variance 0.58, against 114 on the walnut frame and 3751 on the embroidered board. High-pass std is about 0.42/255 at sigma 2 px, and only about 37 luminance levels span the 936x1000 px field. That is correct for the hand-off and must not be altered, since it has to match the live game, but it is the area most likely to band or macroblock in an 8-bit H.264 delivery, especially during the S24-S26 dissolve. Encode the master at 10-bit (or 8-bit with tune=grain or film plus high AQ strength), and add this field to the G12 check on the encoded file, not only the PNG. Do not add grain to the master PNG; that would break the bit match with the live game.

P4 (downstream continuity, record in rects.json/report): give S24/S25 a parchment frequency target, for example: field high-pass std about 0.4/255 at sigma 2 px, mean luminance about 203/255, and the foxing-speck density. The tapestry leaf that lands on the card must then be low-passed and graded to it before the dissolve, or the hand-off will read as a pop from sharp textile to soft bitmap. Also note the light target. I measured no card drop shadow on the board (water luminance is flat at about 85 from x=1230 outward), and the game frame has flat, even lighting with no raking light. The cinematic's raking light therefore has to be fully graded out by the start of the dissolve.

P5 (minor hygiene): every PNG, including the keyframe, the captures and the mattes, carries no colour metadata at all (only IHDR, IDAT and IEND). Add an sRGB chunk, or document 'untagged = sRGB, Godot Compatibility sRGB-space blend' in rects.json, so Blender, AE or Nuke do not reinterpret them when the mattes are relit. Flag the final encode explicitly as BT.709 with full or limited range matched to how the game presents on device.
praise: Through the material and light lens, f1983 is what a hand-off frame should be. I checked it myself at 100 % and with contrast-stretched and x16 residual crops of all four card corners, the field centre, and both the 16:9 and 4:3 buckets. The rebuilt blank parchment cannot be told from the game's own card. The foxing specks, mottling, warm cream tone, inner dark line, walnut frame grain and brass corners are all intact, with no halo or seam. Row and column residual profiles across the replacement boundary stay at or below 0.06/255. There is no luminance step above 0.5/255 anywhere in the field profiles, and the contrast-stretched field shows no rectangle, tiling or banding edge. Outside the card the frame is bit-identical to the live capture: I re-measured the changed bbox as x266-1187/y357-1343 in 16:9 and x213-950/y285-1074 in 4:3, both strictly inside the parchment field. The 3D board in the SwiftShader capture is native 2560 and crisp. The embroidered hexes, valance couching and thread fringe, lion carving and candle wax all match the 1920 reference look, and the concentric contour rings on the shields are part of the game's own art, not capture banding. The chrome mattes are true straight-alpha layers drawn from source textures: composited over magenta, the valance tassels, banner fringe, lion and card corner show no dark or light fringing. Only the candle flame/unlit split layers need a small exactness pass before the relight shots.
